summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and gastroparesis was admitted for acute on chronic abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and uncontrolled hyperglycemia. She presented with a blood glucose of 456 and elevated liver enzymes but no severe acidosis. Her symptoms were attributed to poor glycemic control and exacerbation of gastroparesis, possibly influenced by dietary indiscretion. She was managed with insulin regimen adjustments—increasing glargine to 12 units in the morning and 15 at night, and setting mealtime humalog to 5 units before each meal. She continued treatment for MSSA bacteremia with cefazolin and vancomycin locks, and for Clostridium difficile with metronidazole. An ultrasound showed gallbladder wall thickening without acute cholecystitis, and a right upper extremity ultrasound confirmed a patent fistula with no abscess despite localized tenderness. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics, adhere to a low-fat, small-meal diet, monitor blood glucose, and follow up with endocrinology and gastroenterology.
